idiom_name: async/await with Task and suspension points
implementation_notes: SE-0296 makes asynchronous functions part of the language: the compiler turns an async function into a state machine, await marks a potential suspension point, and when the awaited operation completes the concurrency runtime resumes the task where it left off, so completion dispatch is the runtime's job. Completion sources for real I/O come from frameworks and libraries (URLSession, DispatchIO, swift-nio), and callback APIs are bridged into await with withCheckedContinuation or withCheckedThrowingContinuation. The classic completion-handler style remains appropriate when wrapping APIs that predate Swift concurrency.
pitfalls: Suspension points break atomicity: state protected by a serial queue can be interleaved at every await, so shared state needs actor isolation.
Never block a thread owned by the cooperative pool (no semaphores or sleeps inside a task); use explicit suspension or hand work to a DispatchQueue.
Cancellation is cooperative: it propagates to child tasks and must be checked with Task.isCancelled or try Task.checkCancellation().
